Package io.webagent4j.workflow

Interface IWorkflowCondition

public interface IWorkflowCondition
Simple, deterministic, side-effect-free declarative condition guarding a workflow step.

WorkflowConditions supplies the built-in, intentionally small declarative condition set (see docs/workflow.md#conditions for the full list and their missing-variable semantics) - it is not an arbitrary Predicate or scripting facade. Unlike IWorkflowStep, this interface is a trusted Java extension point: a caller may implement it directly. Every method here is treated as caller-supplied code, and WorkflowEngine handles evaluate(io.webagent4j.workflow.IWorkflowVariables) and describe() defensively at execution time - a RuntimeException from either, or a null describe() result, becomes a structured CONDITION_EVALUATION_FAILED failure rather than propagating - and this applies equally when the condition is wrapped by a WorkflowConditions combinator (not, allOf, anyOf): a combinator preserves a wrapped condition's throwing or null describe() result rather than normalizing it into ordinary composed text - but a custom implementation is still expected to honor the contracts documented on each method below, and to redact/omit any secret value it knows about from describe()'s own text (the engine additionally redacts every currently-known secret out of a stored description as defense in depth, but that is not a substitute for a condition never emitting one intentionally). referencedVariables() is validated separately and earlier, at Workflow.Builder#build() - definition time, before any execution exists: a null result, a result containing null, or a RuntimeException from that method is a definition error and throws IllegalArgumentException directly, never a WorkflowResult.

evaluate(io.webagent4j.workflow.IWorkflowVariables) must never mutate variables or any external state, and must return the same result for the same variable values every time it is called.

  • Method Details

    • evaluate

      boolean evaluate(IWorkflowVariables variables)
      Evaluates this condition against the current execution variables.
      Throws:
      WorkflowVariableMissingException - if the condition requires a variable that is not present (fail-closed: only exists/notExists tolerate a missing variable)

    • describe

      String describe()
      Returns a safe, human-readable description - never a secret value. A description stored in a WorkflowConditionResult is always redacted against every currently-known secret and length-bounded by WorkflowEngine before it is stored. A caller invoking this method directly, outside WorkflowEngine, receives the condition's own text as-is: for a built-in condition, that is a crash-safe rendering of any public literal it compares against, deliberately not yet bounded, since bounding it before the engine's execution-time redaction could otherwise truncate a secret mid-value and leak a partial fragment.

    • referencedVariables

      Set<WorkflowVariable<?>> referencedVariables()
      Returns every variable this condition reads, used by Workflow.Builder.build() to statically reject a condition that references a variable that is neither a declared input nor produced by an earlier step (see docs/workflow.md#conditions). Must never be null and must never contain a null element; Workflow.Builder.build() rejects a condition whose metadata violates either as a definition error.
